title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, point out 'this one' and 'that one', bargain politely and buy clothes and gifts.
intro:
Shopping in Sindh's bazaars is social: you'll be offered tea, asked where you're from, and expected to bargain a little — with a smile. The key question is **هي ڪيترن جو آهي؟** (hī ketiran jo āhe?) 'How much is this?' — literally 'this is of how many (rupees)?'.

This unit also sorts out Sindhi's demonstratives: **هي / هيءَ** (this), **هو / هوءَ** (that, over there) and **اهو / اها** (that, it).

Refers to something mentioned or a bit away. اها uhā (f), اهي uhe (pl).

phrases.en: Bring it down a bit, brother.

phrases.roman: moṃ khe hūa nīrī qamīsa ɗekhāryo.

grammar.title: Demonstratives: this, that and 'this one'
grammar.body:
Sindhi has three sets of demonstratives:

**Near — 'this, these'**: هي hī (general), with the more specific written forms **هيءُ** hīu (m) and **هيءَ** hīa (f). Oblique: **هن** hin; plural oblique **هنن** hinan. Also اِهو iho / اِها ihā 'this one here'.
**Far — 'that, those (over there)'**: **هو** hū (m), **هوءَ** hūa (f). Oblique **هن** hun; plural **هنن** hunan.
**Referring — 'that, it'**: **اهو** uho (m), **اها** uhā (f), **اهي** uhe (pl) — for things just mentioned or a little away. Oblique **ان** un, plural **انهن** unhan.

They work as adjectives too: هيءَ قميص 'this shirt', هن دڪان ۾ 'in this shop', ان ڏينهن 'that day'.

**'This one / that one'**: add **وارو** (agreeing: واري f, وارا pl): هي وارو 'this one', ڳاڙهي واري 'the red one (f)'.

examples.native: هن دڪان ۾ سڀ ڪجهه سستو آهي.
examples.roman: hin dukāna meṃ sabhu kujhu sasto āhe.
examples.en: Everything in this shop is cheap.
That's true. (lit. that matter is correct)

examples.native: مون کي ڪاري واري جتي گهرجي.
examples.roman: moṃ khe kārī vārī jutī ghurje.
examples.en: I want the black shoe (the black one).

grammar.title: Prices and bargaining
grammar.body:
The commonest way to ask a price is **ڪيترن جو؟** — 'of how many (rupees)?': هي ڪيترن جو آهي؟ (masculine item), هيءَ ڪيترن جي آهي؟ (feminine item), هي ڪيترن جا آهن؟ (plural). You can also ask **قيمت ڪيتري آهي؟** 'what's the price?' or, at the end, **ڪيترا پئسا ٿيا؟** 'how much does it come to?'

Prices: number + **رپيا** (rupayā, plural): پنج سؤ رپيا '500 rupees', هڪ هزار رپيا '1,000 rupees'.

**Bargaining** phrases: ٿورو گهٽ ڪريو 'make it a bit less', آخري قيمت؟ 'final price?', ايترو نه 'not that much', ٺيڪ آهي، ڏيو 'OK, give it to me'. Keep it friendly — a smile and ادا / سائين go a long way.

examples.native: اها ٽوپي پنج سؤ رپين جي آهي.
examples.roman: uhā ṭopī panja sau rupayan jī āhe.

examples.en: Give it (to me) for three hundred.

examples.native: ايترو نه، سائين! ٻه سؤ ٺيڪ آهي.
examples.roman: etiro na, sāīṃ! ɓa sau ṭhīku āhe.
examples.en: Not that much, sir! Two hundred is fine.

dialogue.title: Buying a Sindhi topi
dialogue.setting: John is at a stall in Hyderabad's Shahi Bazaar.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.en: Come, sir, what do you need?

lines.native: مون کي سنڌي ٽوپي گهرجي. هيءَ ڪيترن جي آهي؟
lines.speaker: John
lines.roman: moṃ khe sindhī ṭopī ghurje. hīa ketiran jī āhe?
lines.en: I want a Sindhi cap. How much is this one?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: هيءَ هٿ جي ڀرت واري آهي — ٻارهن سؤ.
lines.roman: hīa hatha jī bharata vārī āhe — ɓārahaṃ sau.
lines.en: This one is hand-embroidered — twelve hundred.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: ٻارهن سؤ؟ تمام مهانگي آهي! ٿورو گهٽ ڪريو.
lines.roman: ɓārahaṃ sau? tamām mahāngī āhe! thoro ghaṭu karyo.
lines.en: Twelve hundred? That's very expensive! Bring it down a bit.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: توهان مهمان آهيو. هڪ هزار ڏيو.
lines.roman: tavhāṃ mehmānu āhyo. hiku hazāru ɗiyo.
lines.en: You're a guest. Give me a thousand.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: نو سؤ، آخري قيمت. ۽ اجرڪ به ڏسو، ڏاڍي سهڻي آهي.
lines.roman: nava sau, āxirī qīmata. ai ajraka bi ɗiso, ɗāḍhī sohaṇī āhe.
lines.en: Nine hundred, final price. And look at the ajrak too, it's lovely.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: چڱو، نو سؤ. اجرڪ ڪنهن ٻئي ڏينهن.
lines.roman: chaṅgo, nava sau. ajraka kanhin ɓie ɗīṃha.
lines.en: OK, nine hundred. The ajrak another day.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ٺيڪ آهي سائين. مبارڪ هجي! وري اچجو.
lines.roman: ṭhīku āhe sāīṃ. mubārak huje! varī achijo.
lines.en: Alright sir. Congratulations (on your purchase)! Do come again.

culture: Hyderabad's **Shahi Bazaar** is one of the longest bazaars in South Asia, running from the old fort through the heart of the city, and the city is famous across Pakistan for its glass **bangles** (چوڙيون). Sindhi crafts include ajrak printing, **ralli** (رلي) patchwork quilts, mirror-work embroidery (ڀرت), lacquered woodwork from Hala, and Thari handloom. Bargaining is normal in markets and with rickshaws, but not in malls, pharmacies or fixed-price shops.
